summary: Prove you understand how the Model Context Protocol works: its hosts, clients, servers, and tools, the message flow and primitives that connect them, and the trust boundaries that keep the connection safe.
audience: AI engineers, platform engineers, and AI governance professionals who connect agents to external systems and need to reason about how the protocol works and how its components communicate.
recommendedExperience: Foundational knowledge of JSON-RPC or a similar message-based protocol
Experience calling LLM APIs such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or a local model
Understanding of agentic patterns such as tool use and the think-act-observe loop
Basic security literacy: API keys, OAuth 2.1, token handling, and authentication headers
Ability to read an MCP server manifest and its capability definitions

domains.name: MCP Fundamentals
objectives: Explain the purpose and scope of the Model Context Protocol and the integration problem it standardizes
Describe the core MCP concepts and the roles of hosts, clients, servers, and tools
Reason about the interoperability and value of one open protocol over per-system custom integrations

domains.name: Architecture and Components
objectives: Read the schemas and structured data that define MCP messages, capabilities, and manifests
Distinguish the responsibilities of MCP hosts, clients, and servers and how they are wired together
Trace the model interaction flow from a user request through a client to a server and back

domains.name: Interactions and Execution
objectives: Apply the request, response, and notification interaction patterns and handle their results
Handle protocol and tool errors, including malformed requests and failed executions
Walk the tool invocation lifecycle from discovery through call to result
Identify the protocol primitives such as tools, resources, prompts, sampling, and roots and how they are used

domains.name: Security and Governance
objectives: Locate the trust boundaries between host, client, server, and the tools a server exposes
Apply permissions and consent so a user approves what a server may see and do
Choose risk and safety controls against tool poisoning, injection, and over-broad access
Design auditability and observability so protocol activity can be traced and reviewed

domains.name: Use Cases and Ecosystem
objectives: Map the roles, responsibilities, and adoption patterns of teams deploying MCP
Select operational use cases where MCP connects agents to real systems
Reason about ecosystem and portability across MCP clients, servers, gateways, and registries

deepDives.label: MCP Fundamentals
deepDives.reason: Build a stateless MCP request contract from first principles

deepDives.label: Building an MCP Server
deepDives.reason: Implement a server that exposes tools and capabilities

deepDives.label: Building an MCP Client
deepDives.reason: Implement a client that discovers and calls tools

deepDives.label: MCP Security and OAuth 2.1
deepDives.reason: Apply permissions and token handling across the trust boundary

deepDives.label: MCP Tool Poisoning
deepDives.reason: Recognize and defend against malicious tool descriptions
